questions.prompt: Squaring √(x + 7) = x - 5 gives x + 7 = (x - 5)², with solutions x = 9 and x = 2. Squaring cannot tell √(x + 7) from -√(x + 7). At x = 2, the line y = x - 5 meets which graph?
questions.prompt_markup: Squaring √(x + 7) = x - 5 gives x + 7 = (x - 5)², with solutions x = 9 and x = 2. Squaring cannot tell √(x + 7) from -√(x + 7). At x = 2, the line y = x - 5 meets which graph?
questions.grading_note: At x = 2, x - 5 = -3 = -√9, so the line meets y = -√(x + 7); the original equation uses +√, so x = 2 is extraneous. At x = 9 the line meets y = √(x + 7).

questions.prompt: Why does √(x - 1) + 5 = 2 have no solution, in terms of the graphs of y = √(x - 1) + 5 and y = 2?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does √(x - 1) + 5 = 2 have no solution, in terms of the graphs of y = √(x - 1) + 5 and y = 2?

choices.text: y = √(x - 1) + 5 is always below the line y = 2, so the graphs never meet.
The graph of y = √(x - 1) + 5 is not defined for any x, so there is nothing to meet y = 2.
The graphs meet at x = 10, because squaring √(x - 1) = -3 gives x = 10.
y = √(x - 1) + 5 is always at least 5 (a square root is never negative), so it never meets the line y = 2.

questions.correct_answer: y = √(x - 1) + 5 is always at least 5 (a square root is never negative), so it never meets the line y = 2.
questions.grading_note: The radical graph starts at (1, 5) and rises. The others use the extraneous x = 10 (√9 + 5 = 8 ≠ 2), reverse the position, or misstate the domain (x ≥ 1).
